created_roles.name: GitHub Data Researcher
created_roles.description: Open-source ecosystem analyst fluent in the GitHub REST API and its quirks (redirects for renamed repos, 404 on releases/latest, pre-release exclusion). Owns the top-5 selection and every raw number.
created_roles.prompt: You are a senior open-source analyst. Task: find the 5 most-starred open-source LLM/AI multi-agent orchestration frameworks on GitHub and get stars and latest release date from the GitHub API. Method: (0) Write the call budget first: about 15 /repos calls plus 7 releases/latest calls = 22; read X-RateLimit-Remaining and stop to report if it is below the need. (1) Use web_search to collect 10-15 candidates (e.g. microsoft/autogen, crewAIInc/crewAI, langchain-ai/langgraph, MetaGPT, openai/openai-agents-python, camel-ai/camel, OpenBMB/ChatDev, agno-agi/agno, huggingface/smolagents, microsoft/semantic-kernel, OpenHands, AutoGPT) and confirm each current owner/name. (2) For each, fetch https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo} with github_api_fetch (or fetch_url) and read full_name, stargazers_count, license.spdx_id, archived, html_url, description. Never use a number from memory or a snippet. (3) Apply the inclusion rule: self-described agent/multi-agent orchestration framework or SDK, OSI license, not archived, not an awesome-list/tutorial/end-user app, not a general LLM library like LangChain; log borderline decisions with reasons. (4) Rank by stars; for the top 7 call https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/releases/latest and read tag_name, published_at, html_url. On 404 or no Release object, exclude the repo, note it and take the next candidate; if more than 2 of the top 7 are skipped, widen the pool. releases/latest ignores drafts and pre-releases; say so. On a 403 rate-limit, stop and report it rather than guessing. (5) Stop at 5 valid repos. Output the top-5 table, the candidate pool log, the budget (planned vs actual) with raw evidence, and the UTC retrieval timestamp. If the API cannot be reached, fall back to the repo and releases web pages and label those rows 'web-page fallback, not API'. Check that every digit matches the response you read.
created_roles.goal: Deliver a correct, timestamped table of the 5 most-starred open-source multi-agent frameworks with API-sourced stars and latest-release published date, plus a documented candidate pool and API call budget.
responsibilities: Write the API call budget before fetching (planned calls, rate-limit check via X-RateLimit-Remaining)
Build a candidate pool of 10-15 LLM/AI multi-agent orchestration repos using web_search
Call GET /repos/{owner}/{repo} for each candidate: full_name, stargazers_count, license, archived, html_url, description
Rank by stars, apply the inclusion rule, record excluded candidates with reasons
For the top 7 call GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/releases/latest for tag_name, published_at, html_url
Handle 404, archived repos, redirects and 403 rate limits per the stated rules
Record the UTC retrieval timestamp and the exact URL of every call

markdown table: candidate | stars | included? | reason | rank
code block: planned vs actual call count, then key JSON fields per call (full_name, stargazers_count, tag_name, published_at, license.spdx_id)

## Thought
The work is a short pipeline: find the top 5, fetch, tabulate, chart, write, verify, send. The main risks are the selection and the delivery. GitHub has no "multi-agent framework" category, so the plan uses a stated candidate pool and inclusion rule, and QA checks that nothing excluded outranks rank 5. Star counts drift and `releases/latest` can 404 or skip pre-releases, so every number carries a timestamp and gets an independent re-check. The unauthenticated API limit is 60 requests/hour, so the plan budgets calls (about 22 for the Researcher, about 13 for QA). A 403 is recorded as "unverified", never PASS. Email needs an account that only the user can supply, so the plan ends either with a confirmed send or with an `.eml` and "NOT SENT". Following the reviewer, the prose target drops to 500–600 words once the reference list and chart are budgeted. QA gets its own tools, including an independent page count. The fix loop and the send gate are written out explicitly.

## Requirements:
R1: Find the 5 most-starred open-source multi-agent frameworks (LLM/AI-agent orchestration frameworks) on GitHub, using a documented candidate pool and inclusion rule.
R2: Get each framework's star count (`stargazers_count`) from the GitHub API.
R3: Get each framework's latest release date (`published_at` of `releases/latest`) from the GitHub API.
R4: Put the data in a spreadsheet (Excel .xlsx file).
R5: Make a chart of the data (stars per framework, latest release date shown).
R6: Write a 2-page Word (.docx) report that includes the chart and the data.
R7: Include citations in the report: numbered in-text references and a reference list linking to the GitHub repos and the GitHub API endpoints used.
R8: Email the report to test@example.com.
R9: (implied) Make the data trustworthy: record the retrieval timestamp, confirm the open-source license, and have a role that did not produce the artifacts verify numbers, rank, files, page count and citations before sending.
R10: Planning (implied): carry out the delivery planning before staffing and sending. That means a stated API call budget, the inclusion rule, the fix loop and the send gate, and a risk list that is reported in the final memo.

## Givens and Assumptions:
- given: 5 frameworks; fields = stars + latest release date; outputs = .xlsx, chart, 2-page .docx, email to test@example.com.
- derived: spreadsheet = 5 repos × 10 columns (rank, repo, stars, latest tag, published_at, license, repo URL, stars API URL, release API URL, retrieved_at) = 50 data cells plus a header row.
- derived: reference list = 5 repo refs + 5 endpoint refs (one per repo, covering `/repos/{o}/{r}` and `/releases/latest`) + 1 GitHub REST docs ref = 11 references, set at 9pt (~11 lines ≈ 0.2 page).
- derived: 2-page text budget ≈ 2 × 500 = 1000 words. Subtract the chart (~0.35 page ≈ 175), the table and caption (~0.15 page ≈ 75), the reference list (~0.2 page ≈ 100) and the title and headings (~50): 1000 − 175 − 75 − 100 − 50 = 600. Prose target is 500–600 words.
- derived: API budget, Researcher = 15 `/repos` calls + 7 `releases/latest` calls = 22. QA = 5 + 5 + 3 (ranks 6–7 plus the highest rule-excluded candidate) = 13. A single pass = 35, under the 60/hour limit. A rerun of step 1 and 4 would reach about 70, so it needs a token or a wait.
- assumption: "Most-starred" is judged within a documented pool of 10–15 repos (AutoGen, CrewAI, LangGraph, MetaGPT, OpenAI Agents SDK, CAMEL, ChatDev, Agno, smolagents, Semantic Kernel, OpenHands, AutoGPT, etc.) found with web_search. It is not an exhaustive scan.
- assumption: Inclusion rule: the repo describes itself as an agent or multi-agent orchestration framework or SDK, has an OSI-approved license, and is not archived, an awesome-list, a tutorial or a single-purpose end-user app. General LLM libraries (e.g. LangChain) are excluded. Borderline calls are logged with reasons.
- assumption: If `releases/latest` returns 404, the repo is skipped and the next candidate is used. If more than 2 of the top 7 are skipped, the pool is widened and step 1 re-run.
- assumption: `releases/latest` excludes drafts and pre-releases. The report states this. Renamed repos are cited under the API's canonical `full_name`.
- assumption: The snapshot is the UTC time of the run. QA tolerance is ±1% on stars; tags and dates must match exactly.
- assumption: The email attaches the .docx and .xlsx, with the chart embedded in the report and a 3–5 line body.
- assumption: Default layout (Calibri 11 for body, 9pt references, 1" margins), since no house style was given.

## Open Questions:
- question: Which sender account or SMTP/email service, and which credentials, send the mail to test@example.com? | assumption: not settled. This is the user's to supply. The plan uses the `send_email` tool if it is filled. If it is not, an `.eml` is produced and the status is "NOT SENT".
- question: Is a GitHub personal access token available for the API? | assumption: not settled. This is the user's to supply. If none is supplied, calls are unauthenticated (60/hour) and kept under budget.
- question: Does `fetch_url` return raw JSON from api.github.com? | assumption: yes. If it does not, rows from web pages are labelled "web-page fallback, not API" and QA records the deviation.

## Risks and Decisions:
- **Delivery depends on the user:** the email tool and credentials may not be filled. Step 5 then ends with an `.eml` and a "NOT SENT" status that the summariser repeats. It is never reported as sent.
- **Send gate and fix loop:** nothing is sent unless QA says PASS. On FAIL, the named step is redone. If the data or chart changed, step 3 is redone before step 4 is repeated. Step 5 runs only after a PASS. If QA can't PASS after two rounds, stop and report the open defects instead of sending.
- **No official "multi-agent framework" category on GitHub:** the ranking is pool-based. Mitigation: a pool of 10–15 repos, a logged inclusion rule, and the QA check on ranks 6–7 and the highest rule-excluded candidate. If a borderline repo (OpenHands, AutoGPT) would enter the top 5, the Researcher logs the call and the reason, and the report states it.
- **Release-date edge cases:** `releases/latest` returns 404 for tag-only repos and skips pre-releases and drafts, so a repo can look inactive. Skip 404 repos and take the next candidate. If more than 2 of the top 7 are skipped, widen the pool and re-run step 1.
- **API budget:** a single pass is about 35 calls (Researcher 22, QA 13), under 60/hour. A re-run could pass 60, so a token (if the user supplies one) or a wait is needed. A 403 means the check is UNVERIFIED, and the summariser reports it.
- **Star drift between steps 1 and 4:** ±1% applies. If the rank order of the top 5 changes between fetches, re-run step 1 and the steps after it.
- **Page-count control:** the reference list and chart are budgeted (prose 500–600 words, references at 9pt). If the docx is not exactly 2 pages, adjust prose or chart height. If no PDF converter exists, the count is an estimate, both the Author and QA label it so, and the final memo says the page check was not independently measured.

## Thought
The task is a short data pipeline: select, fetch, tabulate, chart, write, verify, send. The risks are the selection and the delivery. "Most-starred multi-agent framework" has no official GitHub category, so I need a stated candidate pool and inclusion rule, and a check that no excluded candidate outranks the fifth. Star counts drift and `releases/latest` can return 404 or skip pre-releases, so every number needs a retrieval timestamp and an independent re-check. Sending email needs an email tool and credentials that only the user can supply. If that tool is not filled, the plan ends with a ready-to-send `.eml` and an explicit "NOT SENT" status, never a claim of success. The summariser has no tools, so the Report Author builds the .docx and sends the email, the Analyst builds the .xlsx and chart, and a separate QA Reviewer verifies.

## Requirements:
R1: Identify the 5 most-starred open-source multi-agent frameworks (LLM/AI-agent orchestration frameworks) on GitHub, with a documented candidate pool and inclusion rule.
R2: Get each framework's star count (`stargazers_count`) from the GitHub API.
R3: Get each framework's latest release date from the GitHub API (`published_at` of `releases/latest`).
R4: Put the data in a spreadsheet (Excel .xlsx file).
R5: Make a chart of the data (stars per framework, release dates shown).
R6: Write a 2-page Word (.docx) report that includes the chart and the data.
R7: Include citations in the report: in-text numbered references and a reference list linking to the GitHub repos and the GitHub API endpoints used.
R8: Email the report to test@example.com.
R9: (implied) Make the data trustworthy: record the retrieval timestamp, confirm the open-source license, and have a different role verify numbers, rank, files, page count and citations before sending.

## Givens and Assumptions:
- given: 5 frameworks; fields = stars + latest release date; outputs = .xlsx, chart, 2-page .docx, email to test@example.com.
- derived: spreadsheet size = 5 repos × about 9 columns (rank, repo, stars, latest tag, published_at, license, repo URL, API URL, retrieved_at) = 45 data cells plus a header.
- derived: 2-page text budget ≈ 2 pages × ~500 words = 1000 words. Subtract the chart (~0.35 page ≈ 175 words) and the 5-row table plus caption (~0.15 page ≈ 75 words) → about 750 words of prose, with a tolerance of 650–800.
- derived: candidate pool of at least 10 repos, so that rank 6 and beyond can be checked against rank 5. Surplus candidates = 10 − 5 = 5 or more.
- assumption: "Most-starred" is judged within a documented candidate pool of about 10–15 repos. The pool comes from web_search plus the known names (AutoGen, CrewAI, LangGraph, MetaGPT, OpenAI Agents SDK, CAMEL, ChatDev, Agno, smolagents, Semantic Kernel, OpenHands, AutoGPT, etc.). It is not an exhaustive scan of GitHub, which has no category API.
- assumption: Inclusion rule: the repo describes itself as an agent or multi-agent orchestration framework or SDK, has an OSI-approved license, and is not an awesome-list, tutorial, or single-purpose end-user app. General LLM libraries (e.g. LangChain) are excluded. Borderline cases are listed with the reason for the decision.
- assumption: If `releases/latest` returns 404 (the repo only has tags) or the repo is archived, that repo is skipped and the next-ranked candidate is used. The exclusion is noted in the report.
- assumption: `releases/latest` excludes drafts and pre-releases by design, and this is stated in the report's method note. Renamed or moved repos (e.g. MetaGPT, AutoGen) are cited under their canonical `full_name` returned by the API.
- assumption: Snapshot date is the day of the run (UTC). Stars are quoted as of the retrieval timestamp. QA tolerance on re-fetch is ±1% on stars because counts drift; release dates must match exactly.
- assumption: The email attaches the .docx (the report) and the .xlsx, with the chart embedded in the report. The body is a 3–5 line summary.
- assumption: Fonts and layout use defaults (Calibri 11, A4 or Letter, 1" margins), since no house style was given.

## Open Questions:
- question: Which sender account or SMTP/email service, and with what credentials, will be used to send to test@example.com? | assumption: an email-sending tool from the pool is used with whatever account it is configured with. If none is filled, a complete `.eml` with attachments is produced and the result is reported as "NOT SENT".
- question: Does `fetch_url` return raw JSON from api.github.com, and is the unauthenticated rate limit (60 requests/hour) enough? | assumption: yes, about 25 calls are needed. - **No official "multi-agent framework" category on GitHub:** the ranking is pool-based and may miss a niche repo. Decision point: if a borderline repo such as OpenHands or AutoGPT would enter the top 5, the Researcher records the call and the reason, and the report states it.

## Risks and Decisions:
- **Delivery depends on the user:** the email tool and credentials may not be filled. Step 5 then ends with an `.eml` and a "NOT SENT" status that the summariser repeats. It is never reported as sent.
- **Send gate and fix loop:** nothing is sent unless QA says PASS. On FAIL, the named step is redone. If the data or chart changed, step 3 is redone before step 4 is repeated. Step 5 runs only after a PASS. If QA can't PASS after two rounds, stop and report the open defects instead of sending.
- **No official "multi-agent framework" category on GitHub:** the ranking is pool-based. Mitigation: a pool of 10–15 repos, a logged inclusion rule, and the QA check on ranks 6–7 and the highest rule-excluded candidate. If a borderline repo (OpenHands, AutoGPT) would enter the top 5, the Researcher logs the call and the reason, and the report states it.
- **Release-date edge cases:** `releases/latest` returns 404 for tag-only repos and skips pre-releases and drafts, so a repo can look inactive. Skip 404 repos and take the next candidate. If more than 2 of the top 7 are skipped, widen the pool and re-run step 1.
- **API budget:** a single pass is about 35 calls (Researcher 22, QA 13), under 60/hour. A re-run could pass 60, so a token (if the user supplies one) or a wait is needed. A 403 means the check is UNVERIFIED, and the summariser reports it.
- **Star drift between steps 1 and 4:** ±1% applies. If the rank order of the top 5 changes between fetches, re-run step 1 and the steps after it.
- **Page-count control:** the reference list and chart are budgeted (prose 500–600 words, references at 9pt). If the docx is not exactly 2 pages, adjust prose or chart height. If no PDF converter exists, the count is an estimate, both the Author and QA label it so, and the final memo says the page check was not independently measured.

requirements.R1: Find the 5 most-starred open-source multi-agent frameworks (LLM/AI-agent orchestration frameworks) on GitHub, using a documented candidate pool and inclusion rule.
requirements.R2: Get each framework's star count (`stargazers_count`) from the GitHub API.

requirements.R5: Make a chart of the data (stars per framework, latest release date shown).
requirements.R6: Write a 2-page Word (.docx) report that includes the chart and the data.
requirements.R7: Include citations in the report: numbered in-text references and a reference list linking to the GitHub repos and the GitHub API endpoints used.
requirements.R9: (implied) Make the data trustworthy: record the retrieval timestamp, confirm the open-source license, and have a role that did not produce the artifacts verify numbers, rank, files, page count and citations before sending.

givens: given: 5 frameworks; fields = stars + latest release date; outputs = .xlsx, chart, 2-page .docx, email to test@example.com.
derived: spreadsheet = 5 repos × 10 columns (rank, repo, stars, latest tag, published_at, license, repo URL, stars API URL, release API URL, retrieved_at) = 50 data cells plus a header row.
derived: reference list = 5 repo refs + 5 endpoint refs (one per repo, covering `/repos/{o}/{r}` and `/releases/latest`) + 1 GitHub REST docs ref = 11 references, set at 9pt (~11 lines ≈ 0.2 page).

derived: 2-page text budget ≈ 2 × 500 = 1000 words. Subtract the chart (~0.35 page ≈ 175), the table and caption (~0.15 page ≈ 75), the reference list (~0.2 page ≈ 100) and the title and headings (~50): 1000 − 175 − 75 − 100 − 50 = 600. Prose target is 500–600 words.

derived: API budget, Researcher = 15 `/repos` calls + 7 `releases/latest` calls = 22. QA = 5 + 5 + 3 (ranks 6–7 plus the highest rule-excluded candidate) = 13. A single pass = 35, under the 60/hour limit. A rerun of step 1 and 4 would reach about 70, so it needs a token or a wait.

assumption: "Most-starred" is judged within a documented pool of 10–15 repos (AutoGen, CrewAI, LangGraph, MetaGPT, OpenAI Agents SDK, CAMEL, ChatDev, Agno, smolagents, Semantic Kernel, OpenHands, AutoGPT, etc.) found with web_search. It is not an exhaustive scan.

assumption: Inclusion rule: the repo describes itself as an agent or multi-agent orchestration framework or SDK, has an OSI-approved license, and is not archived, an awesome-list, a tutorial or a single-purpose end-user app. General LLM libraries (e.g. LangChain) are excluded. Borderline calls are logged with reasons.
assumption: If `releases/latest` returns 404, the repo is skipped and the next candidate is used. If more than 2 of the top 7 are skipped, the pool is widened and step 1 re-run.
assumption: `releases/latest` excludes drafts and pre-releases. The report states this. Renamed repos are cited under the API's canonical `full_name`.
assumption: The snapshot is the UTC time of the run. QA tolerance is ±1% on stars; tags and dates must match exactly.
assumption: The email attaches the .docx and .xlsx, with the chart embedded in the report and a 3–5 line body.
assumption: Default layout (Calibri 11 for body, 9pt references, 1" margins), since no house style was given.
risks: **Delivery depends on the user:** the email tool and credentials may not be filled. Step 5 then ends with an `.eml` and a "NOT SENT" status that the summariser repeats. It is never reported as sent.

**Send gate and fix loop:** nothing is sent unless QA says PASS. On FAIL, the named step is redone. If the data or chart changed, step 3 is redone before step 4 is repeated. Step 5 runs only after a PASS. If QA can't PASS after two rounds, stop and report the open defects instead of sending.

**No official "multi-agent framework" category on GitHub:** the ranking is pool-based. Mitigation: a pool of 10–15 repos, a logged inclusion rule, and the QA check on ranks 6–7 and the highest rule-excluded candidate. If a borderline repo (OpenHands, AutoGPT) would enter the top 5, the Researcher logs the call and the reason, and the report states it.

**Release-date edge cases:** `releases/latest` returns 404 for tag-only repos and skips pre-releases and drafts, so a repo can look inactive. Skip 404 repos and take the next candidate. If more than 2 of the top 7 are skipped, widen the pool and re-run step 1.

**API budget:** a single pass is about 35 calls (Researcher 22, QA 13), under 60/hour. A re-run could pass 60, so a token (if the user supplies one) or a wait is needed. A 403 means the check is UNVERIFIED, and the summariser reports it.
**Star drift between steps 1 and 4:** ±1% applies. If the rank order of the top 5 changes between fetches, re-run step 1 and the steps after it.

**Page-count control:** the reference list and chart are budgeted (prose 500–600 words, references at 9pt). If the docx is not exactly 2 pages, adjust prose or chart height. If no PDF converter exists, the count is an estimate, both the Author and QA label it so, and the final memo says the page check was not independently measured.
